candidates: When a MR modifies the behavior of a public method on a concrete, non-experimental class — even when the bulk of the change is legitimately covered by an experimental-API disclaimer (e.g., changes to `Optimizable` implementations) — flag the concrete-class change explicitly as a BREAKING CHANGE in the changelog and evaluate whether a deprecation period is warranted. The experimental designation of an abstract interface does not automatically extend to long-lived methods on concrete subclasses or sibling classes that predate that experimental warning.
